overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law on April 10, 2012 by entering executive session under Purpose 6 while the seller's representative attorney attended; a fire-chief complaint was declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board convened in executive session for an improper purpose, citing the April 10, 2012 session on a receivership property purchase.
allegations.key_passage: by including Attorney O'Grady while he was acting as the seller's representative on April 10, 2012, the Board improperly entered into executive session and violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged individuals not authorized to attend were present in the April 10, 2012 executive session, namely the seller's representative attorney.
allegations.key_passage: When representatives of the seller of the real property, such as the seller's attorney, are present, Purpose 6 is defeated because there is no need to enter executive session to establish a confidential negotiating position.

allegations.summary: Complainant's later request raised a possible June 21, 2012 executive session on a fire chief contract; AG declined review because it was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this issue in accordance with our policies, as it was not raised in his original complaint against the Board.

allegations.summary: Not alleged in the original complaint, the AG noted that February 21, 2012 and July 26, 2011 executive sessions including the seller's attorneys also violated the law.
allegations.key_passage: the Board, by including Attorneys Parker and/or O'Grady in its February 21, 2012 and July 26, 2011 executive sessions also violated the Open Meeting Law for the same reasons stated in this letter

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

Board members who did not attend the September 11, 2012 training must attend an Open Meeting Law training within ninety days of receipt of the letter, conducted by an approved attorney or organization (or by reviewing the AG's training video).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
